section_2.title: Choose the right English check.
section_2.description: Most students should start with B1 or B2. The result is not a rejection — it helps decide whether to apply now, choose a flexible route, or speak to an adviser before the interview.

card.title: This is not a rejection tool.
card.description: English requirements vary by university, course and interview. Lower scores should not make a student self-reject.
cards: B1/B2: often enough to start exploring foundation-year and flexible routes.
A1/A2 or unsure: speak to an adviser to identify realistic interviews and course options.
Advanced: focus on choosing the right degree, funding and application route.

cards.title: Intermediate interview check
cards.description: For students who can handle everyday English and want to check simple interview, grammar and reading confidence.

questions.question: I ___ interested in studying Business Management.
She ___ to college twice a week.
Choose the best sentence.
options: I have five years of experience in retail.

questions.question: What does “deadline” mean?
options: A final date to complete something

questions.question: I want to study because ___.
options: I want to improve my future

questions.question: “The course includes lectures, workshops and assessments.” What does it include?
Choose the polite interview answer.
options: I am interested and willing to learn.

questions.question: What is “experience”?
options: Something you have done or learned

questions.question: Choose the best sentence.
options: I can attend classes two days per week.

questions.question: “Applicants may be invited to an interview.” What may happen?
If I am accepted, I ___ start in September.
Choose the best word: I am ___ for a new opportunity.
Choose the correct form: My previous job ___ very busy.
“Attendance is expected every week.” What does it mean?
options: You can attend once a year

cards.title: Upper-intermediate check
cards.description: For students who can explain opinions, work experience and goals and want to check degree interview readiness.For students who can explain opinions, work experience and goals and want to check degree interview readiness.

questions.question: Choose the best sentence.
options: Although I work full-time, I can organise my study schedule.
Although I working full-time, I can organise.
I can organise although full-time working.

questions.question: If I had more time, I ___ more research before applying.
“The provider offers additional academic support during the first term.” What is offered?
Choose the most formal phrase.
options: I would like to explain my motivation.

questions.question: The course is suitable for students ___ have work experience.
I want to study business ___ it matches my management experience.
What does “assessment” mean?
options: A task used to judge learning

questions.question: Choose the best answer: “Why this course?”
options: It links to my experience and future career goals.

questions.question: Which sentence is clearest?
options: I managed stock, trained new staff and solved customer issues.
I do many things in job and stuff.
I was doing working there things.

questions.question: The report must be submitted ___ Friday.
“Students are expected to analyse case studies.” What skill is needed?
Choose the correct passive form.
options: The application is reviewed by the admissions team.

questions.question: Choose the best sentence.
options: My goal is to move into project coordination.

questions.question: I have been working in hospitality ___ six years.
“The interview explores motivation, experience and study readiness.” What is discussed?
options: Why you want to study, your background and readiness

questions.question: Choose the strongest phrase.
options: I can give examples from my work experience.

questions.question: What does “progression route” mean?
options: A path to the next study or career step

cards.title: Advanced confidence check
cards.description: For confident speakers checking advanced vocabulary, academic reading and professional interview expression.

questions.question: Choose the most precise sentence.
options: My professional experience has strengthened my ability to evaluate problems and communicate solutions.
My job made me better with things.

questions.question: The phrase “critically evaluate” means ___.
options: judge strengths and weaknesses using evidence

questions.question: Choose the best academic phrase.
options: This suggests a connection between experience and career motivation.

questions.question: If the evidence were stronger, the conclusion ___ more convincing.
“Applicants are expected to justify their course choice.” What should they do?
Choose the correct sentence.
options: Having worked in management, I understand the importance of clear planning.
I having worked and understand planning.

questions.question: Which sentence is strongest for an interview?
options: I can link my work experience to the modules and career outcomes of the course.
I like course because maybe good.
I want study and then see.

questions.question: “The policy may have implications for part-time students.” What are implications?
Choose the best connector: ___ the course is demanding, I am prepared to manage my time.
Choose the best sentence.
options: My long-term aim is to progress into a management role where I can apply analytical and leadership skills.
Long future role good management things.
I want job better because course.

questions.question: “To what extent” questions ask you to ___.
options: consider how far something is true

questions.question: Choose the correct form.
options: The skills I have developed are transferable to higher education.
The skills I developed is transferable.

questions.question: Choose the best phrase.
options: I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my suitability in an interview.
Interview is okay for me maybe.

questions.question: “Students must synthesise ideas from multiple sources.” This means ___.
Choose the best closing interview statement.
options: I am motivated, realistic about the demands of study, and ready to take the next step with support.
